author: xiaokuerz
title: fix(audio): reset stale fade state when GainNode is reused/reconnected

questions.prompt: ResetFadeState sets fadeInState_ to true but collFadeInState_ to false — the opposite polarity. Why is one true and the other false?

options.label: fadeInState_ = true starts a per-stream fade-in to ramp volume up on reconnect (avoids pop); collFadeInState_ = false is the neutral/idle state for collaborative fade-in, which is not desired on reconnect
It's a typo — both should be true for symmetry, otherwise the collaborative fade channel is disabled permanently
fadeInState_ uses true-as-active; collFadeInState_ uses false-as-active — they use opposite boolean conventions for 'fade-in in progress'
collFadeInState_ = false forces a collaborative fade-out to compensate for the per-stream fade-in

questions.explanation: fadeInState_ = true means 'a fade-in is pending, ramp volume up' — desired on reconnect to avoid a pop. collFadeInState_ = false is the neutral state meaning 'no collaborative fade-in pending'. They use the same boolean convention (true = fade-in active), but the collaborative path simply should not trigger a fade-in on reconnect. The asymmetry is intentional, not a polarity inversion.
questions.reinforce: Correct — the asymmetry is intentional: per-stream fade-in is desired on reconnect, collaborative fade-in is not.

questions.prompt: Before this change, CreateGainNode had only the if-branch (create new node) with no else. What happened when CreateGainNode was called for a sessionId that already had a GainNode in idGainMap_?

options.label: Nothing — the existing node was left untouched, keeping whatever stale fade state it had (e.g. DONE_FADEOUT), which could cause it to stay permanently muted after reconnect
A new HpaeGainNode was created and replaced the old entry in idGainMap_, so stale state was never an issue
An assertion fired because the sessionId already existed
The old node was destroyed and idGainMap_[sessionId] became nullptr

questions.explanation: The old code was `if (!SafeGetMap(idGainMap_, sessionId)) { ... create new ... }` — when the node already existed, SafeGetMap returned a non-null shared_ptr, so the condition was false and the entire if-body was skipped. No else branch meant: no action, no reset. The stale fade state (e.g. DONE_FADEOUT from a previous Pause) persisted on the reused node, causing SignalProcess to keep silencing every frame — the exact bug this PR fixes.
questions.reinforce: Correct — the missing else branch was the root cause: reused nodes kept stale DONE_FADEOUT and stayed muted.

questions.prompt: CreateGainNode already calls ResetFadeState when it finds an existing node (the else branch in q2). ConnectInputCluster here also calls ResetFadeState on the same node. If both code paths execute for the same session reconnect, what happens?

options.label: ResetFadeState is idempotent — it just re-assigns the same default values (NO_FADEOUT, counters to 0), so calling it twice is harmless, just redundant
The second call triggers a double fade-in because fadeInState_ is set to true twice, doubling the ramp length
The second call corrupts fadeProcessedBytes_ because it resets a counter that was already mid-increment during the first call's fade-in
The second call throws because the node is in an invalid transitional state after the first reset

questions.explanation: ResetFadeState unconditionally sets fadeOutState_ = NO_FADEOUT, fadeInState_ = true, and all counters to 0. It reads no prior state and has no side effects beyond these assignments. Calling it N times produces the same result as calling it once — the second call just overwrites identical values. The double call site likely exists because ConnectInputCluster and CreateGainNode are on different code paths (not all reconnects go through both), so each is defensive.
questions.reinforce: Correct — ResetFadeState is a pure state-reset with no read-modify-write logic, so duplicate calls are idempotent.

questions.prompt: The test sets fadeOutState_ to DONE_FADEOUT, fills a buffer with UT_UNIT_GAIN (non-zero), runs SignalProcess, and asserts the last sample is 0.0f. What does DONE_FADEOUT mean in the SignalProcess logic that causes this?

options.label: DONE_FADEOUT means the fade-out has already completed; SignalProcess treats it as 'stay silent' and zeroes every sample in the output frame
DONE_FADEOUT means the fade-out is about to begin; SignalProcess starts ramping down from unit gain to zero, so the first frame is only partially attenuated
DONE_FADEOUT is an error state; SignalProcess skips processing entirely and the zero is coincidental
DONE_FADEOUT triggers a fade-in-back-up, but the test checks before it completes

questions.explanation: The fade-out lifecycle is: NO_FADEOUT -> (fade-out triggered) -> fading ramp -> DONE_FADEOUT. Once DONE_FADEOUT is reached, the fade-out is complete and the stream should be silent. SignalProcess checks fadeOutState_ and, when it sees DONE_FADEOUT, applies zero gain to every sample — producing silence. This is correct behavior for an actively-paused stream, but a bug when the node is reused without clearing the state, because the 'done' state persists and silences the new stream's data indefinitely.
questions.reinforce: Correct — DONE_FADEOUT is a terminal 'fade-out finished, stay silent' state; SignalProcess zeroes every frame while it persists.

questions.prompt: The comment says 'DONE_FADEOUT left by a Pause'. Walk through the lifecycle: a user Pauses a stream, the fade-out completes, and the state becomes DONE_FADEOUT. Later the same GainNode is reused for a new session (e.g. device switch) without calling ResetFadeState. What is the user-visible symptom?

options.label: Audio is permanently silent on the reused node — SignalProcess zeroes every frame because DONE_FADEOUT persists, and no new fade-in is ever triggered to recover
Audio plays at a gradually decreasing volume — the stale fade-out state continues ramping down from where it left off
Audio plays normally but with an audible pop at the start because fadeInState_ is still false
Audio plays for a few frames then cuts out — the stale totalFadeBytes_ counter eventually triggers a second fade-out

questions.explanation: DONE_FADEOUT is a terminal state — SignalProcess sees it and applies zero gain to every frame indefinitely. It does not 'continue ramping' (the ramp is already done) and it does not self-recover. Without ResetFadeState clearing fadeOutState_ back to NO_FADEOUT, the reused node stays muted permanently. The user hears silence regardless of the actual audio data being fed in. This is why the bug is 'stale state' rather than 'incorrect ramp' — the state machine is stuck in a terminal state from the previous lifecycle.
questions.reinforce: Correct — the node is stuck in a terminal 'stay silent' state from the previous Pause, producing permanent silence on the reused node.

questions.prompt: After ResetFadeState, the test fills a fresh buffer with UT_UNIT_GAIN, runs SignalProcess, and asserts the last sample is NOT 0.0f (EXPECT_NE). The test checks only the last sample of the frame, not the first. Why is the last sample the meaningful one to check?

options.label: After reset, fadeInState_ = true triggers a fade-in ramp — early samples may be near-zero (ramp start) but the last sample of the frame has ramped up to non-zero, proving the node is no longer in 'silence everything' mode
The last sample is checked because SignalProcess processes audio backwards, so the last sample is processed first and is the most reliable indicator
Only the last sample is affected by fade state; all other samples are always passed through unchanged regardless of fade state
Checking the last sample is arbitrary — any sample would give the same result because ResetFadeState disables SignalProcess entirely

questions.explanation: After ResetFadeState, fadeInState_ = true means SignalProcess will apply a fade-in ramp over the frame. The ramp starts from a low (possibly zero) gain and increases. So the first samples might still be zero or near-zero from the ramp start, which would make an EXPECT_NE on the first sample unreliable. The last sample of the frame has the highest gain in the ramp, so it is the most reliable indicator that the 'silence everything' mode (DONE_FADEOUT) is no longer active. The test deliberately picks the last sample to avoid false failures from the fade-in ramp's low-amplitude start.
questions.reinforce: Correct — the last sample avoids false failures from the fade-in ramp's low-amplitude start, while still proving the DONE_FADEOUT silence path is cleared.
